title: Cone Types and Colour Detection
description: The cone mosaic carries three classes of light sensor, and this episode of Focus Cast by focuslinks reads them spec by spec. Learn the tuning of each class: long-wavelength cones peaking near five hundred and sixty nanometres, middle-wavelength cones near five hundred and thirty, and short-wavelength cones near four hundred and twenty. Hear the census of the short-wave class, roughly one in twelve cones or fewer and absent from the foveal centre, and the two design quirks that make colour possible: broad overlap, where any wavelength lights all three sensors in three different proportions, and univariance, where one cone alone reports only how much light it caught, never which kind. Then follow the resolution that colour lives in the ratios between the three catches, so the cones act not as colour meters but as three differently biased witnesses whose disagreement is the evidence. Made for optometry students and practising optometrists who want the sensors of colour explained for the ear.
